boundary.rationale: 1.41 km N-S × 0.81 km E-W ≈ 1.14 km²: Calea Floreasca from Piața Floreasca (market, S) to Str. Gheorghe Țițeica (N), the 'composer streets' villa quarter (Mozart, Chopin, Bach, Verdi, Ceaikovski, Garibaldi) east of it, Parcul/Grădina Floreasca west of it; edges on quiet residential streets (Str. Banul Antonache W, Str. Ramuri Tei/Kepler E, Bd. Lacul Tei S-ish). Sky Tower (137 m) and Promenada lie 600 m north — render as skyline backdrop.

stops.name: DB Global Technology (Deutsche Bank tech centre) — NOT in Floreasca
stops.finding: The DB technology centre opened in 2014 (UpGround/Dimitrie Pompeiu area) and has had its HQ on Bd. Dimitrie Pompeiu since at least 2015 (6,000+ m² on two floors in a building DB sold to Globalworth and leased back); the current careers page lists 6A Dimitrie Pompeiu Blvd, 020337. No source places it in Floreasca Park (Șos. Pipera 43) or at Calea Floreasca 169A (= Floreasca Business Park, tenants Oracle/Xerox/Holcim/GE…).
stops.recommendation: Move chapter `db` (2017) to district `pipera` — the DB building is ~150 m from Hermes Business Campus (luxoft). See bucharest-pipera.md for its route.

research.cross_section: Main N–S artery of the quarter: 2 lanes northbound + 1–2 southbound (OSM lanes 3–5 incl. turn pockets "left|through|through;right"), split into one-way pairs around short islands at Piața Floreasca and Ceaikovski; 50 km/h; kerbside parking lanes (parking=lane) on long stretches; buses 135, 343, 461 (no trolley, no tram)
research.frontage: W side: Piața Floreasca market (S end), Nusco Floreasca 1–2 offices (141-143, 5 lv), Souk (131B), Agora Floreasca mall (111-113), One Tower (151, 16 lv glass, 2020s), Sanador clinic (165), Parcul Floreasca / former Cinema Floreasca park; E side: 3–4-storey 1930s–50s villas and small blocks with shops, cafes and restaurants on the ground floor (Floreasca became a nightlife/food hotspot)
research.trees: mature linden/chestnut rows both sides; park trees on the W side
research.sidewalks: 3–4 m grey pavers (renovated) with cars on the kerb edge in places
research.skyline: Sky Tower (137 m, 37 floors, Romania's tallest) and the Promenada/Floreasca City Center complex 600 m north dominate the view northbound

research.cross_section: mostly one-way single lane, residential; villas + 3–4-storey 1930s blocks

research.frontage: interwar villas (2–3 storeys, stucco, pitched tile roofs, wrought-iron fences) + the C.A. Rosetti school (11) and Maria Rosetti school (3)

top_local_details: Rosetti is NOT on Calea Floreasca — it is in the villa quarter on Str. Garibaldi 11, ~1.2 km north of the old pin.
Garibaldi and most composer streets are narrow ONE-WAY single-lane streets lined with parked cars.
Sky Tower dominates the northbound view: tallest building in Romania (137 m), glass, rounded, lit crown.
Calea Floreasca has buses only (135/343/461) — no tram, no trolleybus.
Floreasca is leafy: lindens and chestnuts over villa gardens; wrought-iron fences.
1930s villas with red tile roofs, stucco in cream/ochre, many restored, some replaced by boutique blocks.
Ground-floor cafes/restaurants and clinics along Calea Floreasca (Sanador, Medlife, Agora).
Piața Floreasca market at the south end of the avenue.
Parcul Floreasca/grădina on the west side with tall trees.
Nusco and One Tower glass offices on the west side of Calea Floreasca.
Mega Image Maison des Chefs, Garanti bank on Calea Floreasca.
School yard fence and kids crossing at 07:45 and 13:00–14:00.
Cars parked on sidewalks everywhere in the villa grid.
Speed humps/raised zebras around schools (verify).
Calea Floreasca splits into one-way pairs around islands at junctions.
Late-evening crowds and valet parking at restaurants (nightlife hotspot).
No high-rise blocks in the villa grid except a few 4–5-storey ones.
Promenada mall and Floreasca Park office campus lie further north.
Lake Floreasca west of the district (strand/sports complex).
Overhead cables and older concrete lamp posts on side streets.
Red seismic-risk plaques on some older blocks.
Hotel Johann Strauss at the corner of Str. Johann Strauss.
Yellow taxis and Bolt/Uber cars idling at restaurants.
Kerbside parking lanes on Calea Floreasca.
Pedestrian signals with countdowns at Ceaikovski.
Embassy residences and guard booths are common in the area.
Calm, low traffic inside the grid; queues only on Calea Floreasca.
Street-name plates are blue with white text.
Gated driveways with sliding metal gates.
Autumn: chestnut leaves pile on the sidewalks.

driving.note: RO:urban default 50; several boulevards signed 60 (OSM maxspeed=60 on Lascăr Catargiu, Magheru, Dorobanți north).

markings.lane_line: white dashed 3 m line / 6 m gap on urban roads (RO standard SR 1848-7), 0.10–0.15 m wide
markings.centre_line: white continuous (single) on 2-lane two-way, double continuous on 4+ lane two-way without median
markings.zebra: white bars 0.5 m wide / 0.5 m gap, parallel to traffic, no side lines; a few school-zone crossings have red infill between the white bars (verify per crossing on refs)
markings.bus_lane: white continuous line with "BUS" text; since 2019 some STB lanes on Magheru axis/Ștefan cel Mare painted red-brown (#9E3B2E) – verify per street
markings.yellow: yellow only for temporary works and kerb no-parking (zig-zag at bus stops)
markings.wear: markings visibly worn/faded on most streets except freshly resurfaced arteries — use 60–80% opacity

kerbs.material: grey concrete kerbstones 15×25 cm (older streets: granite #8C8C8C), kerb height 12–18 cm, often chipped

sidewalks.paving: mix: (a) grey concrete interlocking pavers ("pavele") #A9A59C on renovated boulevards; (b) cracked asphalt #6E6C68 on side streets; (c) 40×40 grey concrete slabs on 1960–80s estates
sidewalks.parking_on_sidewalk: very common: cars half/fully on the sidewalk on side streets, behind metal bollards on boulevards

traffic_lights.model: RO 3-aspect vehicle heads (200/300 mm), black or yellow housing with yellow-black backplates on main arteries, mounted on grey/black poles + overhead mast arms at big junctions; pedestrian 2-aspect (red/green man) with countdown displays on major junctions

street_name_plates.style: blue plate (#1F4E9A) white text "Bulevardul X" + sector number "Sector 1" in smaller text, on building corners or poles

bus_shelter.style: STB/Clear-channel style glass shelters with grey steel frame and backlit ad panel; many stops have only a pole with the yellow STB stop sign + timetable

metro_totem.style: Metrorex entrance: blue square sign with white "M", station name in white on blue; stairs down with grey stone/steel railings

trolleybus_wires.style: pair of copper contact wires 0.6 m apart per direction at ~5.6 m, carried by span wires between steel or concrete poles on both kerbs (often shared with street lamps)

tram_track.style: standard gauge 1435 mm; on boulevards in a central reservation with concrete sleepers/ballast or grass, kerbed and fenced in places; overhead single contact wire on span wires

lamps.boulevard: galvanised/grey steel octagonal poles 10–12 m, single or double arm, LED or older sodium cobra heads (sodium = orange #FFB45A; LED = 4000 K white #F2F0E6); 25–35 m spacing staggered on both kerbs and often in the median
lamps.side_street: 7–9 m grey poles or concrete poles with single arm, ~30 m spacing
lamps.historic: Calea Victoriei: black ornamental cast-iron style lanterns

trees.species: Tilia (linden, dominant on boulevards), Aesculus hippocastanum (horse chestnut), Acer platanoides, Platanus (plane, older avenues), Robinia pseudoacacia (side streets), Celtis; crown 8–14 m

furniture.bike: I'Velo green docks at main squares

buildings.cables: loose telecom cables strung between buildings/poles on side streets
